title: Half-life cohort warmup log and rollout heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is my working scratchpad for a different approach to ramping new model variants: a half-life based cohort warmup. Goal is to provide a compact, tunable schedule that de-risks immediate spikes, gives stable telemetry signal early, and is easy for automation to enforce.

Summary idea:
- Use an exponential ramp defined by a half-life (t1/2) measured in minutes or hours.
- Traffic fraction at time t: f(t) = 1 - 0.5^(t / t1/2) scaled up to target cohort percent. Example: target cohort = 5% and t1/2 = 30m -> after 30m you are at ~2.5% (half of target), after 60m ~3.75%, after 120m ~4.6875%.
- Advantages: smooth growth, predictable curvature, single knob to tune conservatism vs speed.

Planned parameters (example run):
- Target cohort: 5% of global traffic (split by client bucket, not user ID).
- Initial seed: 0.05% traffic for warmup probes for first 10m (sanity + cache warmups).
- t1/2: 30 minutes. Total 90–120m to asymptote near 5%.
- Safety windows: quiet hours (00:00–06:00 PDT) for final jump to >3%.
- Max concurrency cap: 250 concurrent requests to the variant instance pool.

Preflight checklist (must pass before opening ramp):
- [ ] Model pinned in routing config (version tag and hash).
- [ ] Fallback model variant prepared and tested (auto-fallback teardown).
- [ ] Smoke tests: sample prompt set -> identical schema + no nulls.
- [ ] Cost guardrails: expected tokens estimate reviewed with finance.
- [ ] Alerting hooks deployed: latency, error-rate, tail-latency, quality-regression metric.
- [ ] Canary tracing: trace sampling enabled for cohort traffic.
- [ ] Eviction/rollback toggle tested on staging.

Telemetry probes and thresholds (first 2 hours focus):
- Success rate (2xx) for model call: alert if drop > 1.0 percentage point absolute vs baseline in 5m window.
- 95th latency: alert if > baseline + 150ms sustained over 5m.
- Tail e2e (client->response): alert if p99 increases > 500ms.
- Regeneration rate (model retries): alert if > 0.5% absolute.
- Quality probe (sampled evals on golden set): scoring delta > 3% (mismatch rate) -> immediate hold.
- Cost burn: cost per 1k tokens anomaly +25% -> notify finance + PM.

Abort criteria (immediate rollback):
- Any of the above alerts fire AND are persistent for two consecutive 5m windows.
- Critical runtime errors (OOM, panics) reported by infra -> immediate rollback.
- Customer-facing SLA violations (p99 SLO breached by >100ms for >10m).

Operational runbook (quick):
1) Kickoff: post to #deployments with cohort id, expected timeline, linked dashboards and toggles.
2) Seed step: route 0.05% for 10m. Verify traces, caches, no 5xx.
3) Start exponential ramp automation with t1/2=30m to target 5%. Watch the first 3 half-life steps closely (0–90m).
4) At checkpoints (30m, 60m, 90m): run quick quality batch on 200 sampled prompts from golden set.
5) At any alert -> engage SRE + model owner, decide hold vs rollback. If hold, freeze ramp and run mitigations (scale pool, lower concurrency, toggle feature flags).
6) If asymptote reached and metrics stable for 2h, promote cohort to persistent routing rule and schedule slower global rollout.

Notes on instrumentation to add (TODOs):
- Add cohort label to traces and logs (done for http header but not for internal traces).
- Emit a "warmup-stage" metric with binning by minute for easier visualization.
- Synthetic traffic generator to validate t1/2 curve under failure modes.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should t1/2 be client-region aware? (Pros: avoids blast in small critical regions; Cons: complexity + more knobs).
- How to handle high-cost prompts during early ramp? Option: sample-by-prompt-cost and throttle or send to fallback.
- Is golden set scoring fast enough to give timely signal at 30m checkpoints? If not, need lightweight proxies (n-gram overlap heuristics).

Post-release retrospective template (fill after):
- Actual timeline and t1/2 used:
- Total time to reach target:
- Alerts fired (list timestamps + resolution):
- Quality regression results vs golden set:
- Token cost delta and billing impact:
- Lessons learned and next t1/2 recommendation:

Quick links and refs:
- INFR-4213 (rollout automation task)
- PR 998 (routing/feature-flag changes)
- Slack thread: #deployments/INFR-4213 discussion

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Wire up warmup-stage metric -> Grafana panel (Ethan).
- Add trace cohort label to runtime traces (Maya).
- Prototype synthetic generator and run in staging this week (Liam).

Random notes to self: keep t1/2 conservative for first few cross-model flips; we can speed up later when we have consistent score deltas. Consider a morning-end window for final >3% jumps to avoid heavy west-coast traffic.

-- Sofia
